subject: Renewal negotiation: Polylink multi-region Dedicated capacity expansion
messages:
From: Miguel Torres <miguel@polylink.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 Jan 2027 13:12:00 +0100
Subject: Renewal discussion + multi-region capacity questions

Hi Jasmine,

We're coming up on our Dedicated renewal and want to add explicit EU and APAC reserved pools as part of the next term. A few quick items we need to understand before we sign:

- Target latency expectations: can Redwood commit to sub-120ms 95th pctl in EU and sub-150ms 95th pctl in APAC for our standard chat workload?
- Sustained throughput target: we need ~400 requests/min with average responses of ~120 tokens, with room to burst 2x for short windows during business hours.
- Failover behavior: if EU capacity is saturated, will traffic fail over to US? Any cross-region costs or performance impacts?
- Contract mechanics: we prefer a single amendment that adds regional pools and a throughput SLA rather than separate addenda.

Can you share a strawman capacity proposal and what the incremental cost would be? Also looping procurement (procurement@polylink.com) and Anika who handles renewal approvals.

Thanks,
Miguel
Head of Platform Engineering
Polylink Inc.
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Miguel Torres <miguel@polylink.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 Jan 2027 15:03:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion + multi-region capacity questions

Hi Miguel — thanks for the clear list. Happy to run point on this.

Agenda I propose for the week:
1) Quick scoping call to confirm workload characteristics and planned burst windows (30 min)
2) Strawman capacity + SLA appendix from our side (we'll include latency pctl targets, regional pool sizes, and failover semantics)
3) Proposed amendment language and commercial uplift for review by procurement

Deliverables I'll send after the call: initial_capacity_sheet.xlsx and a short SLA_Appendix.pdf. Rishi will draft pricing tiers; Neha will propose amendment term language and ramp schedule.

Proposed times for scoping call: Tue Jan 5 10:00 CET or Wed Jan 6 09:00 CET — which works?

Regards,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: initial_capacity_sheet.xlsx (xlsx)]
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: Miguel Torres <miguel@polylink.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 5 Jan 2027 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion + multi-region capacity questions — pricing + capacity strawman

Miguel / team,

Based on the targets Jasmine outlined and our throughput profiles for similar customers, here's a strawman we can offer (subject to final verification on the scoping call):

- EU reserved pool: 8 A100-equivalent reserved nodes (sustained capacity for ~450 req/min at 120-token avg), includes 2-node burst buffer.
- APAC reserved pool: 6 A100-equivalent reserved nodes, includes 1-node burst buffer.
- Failover model: primary region handles traffic; if capacity reaches 95% for >30s we route overflow to the next region (US) with a transparent flag. Cross-region egress billed as incremental network cost; we can cap cross-region failover costs in the amendment.

SLA proposal (95th/99th planning):
- EU: 95th latency <= 120ms for standard chat (target), financial SLA available at 99.5% availability for requests served from reserved pool.
- APAC: 95th latency <= 150ms, financial SLA at 99.0% (given longer network tails).

Commercials (high-level):
- Incremental monthly commitment: EU pool + APAC pool = equivalent of 14 reserved nodes.
- Discount: 18% off list for a 24-month committed term; 12% for 18-month.
- One-time amendment processing fee waived if signed within 21 days of proposal date.

I'll attach the pricing_grid.csv with node-level math. If Polylink wants stronger failover cost controls, we can add a capped cross-region spend and a mandatory 30-minute maintenance window for burst tests.

—Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pricing_grid.csv (csv)]
From: procurement@polylink.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Miguel Torres <miguel@polylink.com>, Anika Sharma <anika.sharma@polylink.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Jan 2027 08:46:00 +05:30
Subject: Polylink procurement questions: amendment scope, data locality, audit access

Hi Jasmine / Rishi,

Thanks for the strawman. A few procurement/legal items we need clarified before drafting a PO:

1) Data locality & logs: for the EU pool, logs and any PII need to stay within EU physical regions. Can you confirm whether audit logs and request traces will be accessible and retained per our 12-month requirement?
2) Term and early exit: we prefer the shorter 18-month term with a 60-day early-exit clause subject to a financial penalty (X% of remaining commitment). Is that feasible?
3) Cross-region failover: need a hard cap on cross-region egress charges and an SLA around failover correctness (no dropped requests, clear error codes).
4) Security evidence: SOC2 Type II report and network architecture diagram for the proposed dedicated pools (can be redacted).

Attaching a short questionnaire we use for amendments. Please provide answers so procurement can prepare the PO.

Best,
Polylink Procurement Team
[Attachment: procurement_questions.docx (docx)]
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: procurement@polylink.com, Miguel Torres <miguel@polylink.com>
Cc: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 7 Jan 2027 11:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Polylink procurement questions: amendment scope, data locality, audit access

Hi Procurement / Miguel,

Thanks for the list — happy to formalize. Responses in brief and next steps: 

1) Data locality & logs: EU-resident pools will store request logs and traces in EU regions. We can offer 12-month retention for audit logs in the EU archive; access via secure S3 endpoint and audit exports on request.
2) Term & early exit: We can accommodate the 18-month term with an early-exit option. Standard early-exit penalty is 25% of remaining committed spend; we can negotiate to 20% if the PO is signed within 14 days.
3) Cross-region failover: We'll add a capped cross-region egress allocation (suggested cap: $6k/month) and a failover correctness SLA (no more than 0.1% request loss during a failover window). We'll include explicit error code behavior in the SLA appendix.
4) Security evidence: SOC 2 Type II and redacted network diagrams will be attached to the amendment package.

Commercially: If Polylink signs for 18 months, final incremental uplift is adjusted per Rishi's grid (12% discount). For 24 months the economics improve (18% discount). We'll include a 3-month phase-in ramp (50% capacity first 30 days, full allocation by day 90) to avoid sudden cutovers.

I'll prepare an amendment draft and include: SLA_Appendix.pdf, the capped egress clause, and a short failover runbook. DocuSign link will be provided in the next message.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Renewals Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SLA_Appendix.pdf (pdf)]
From: Miguel Torres <miguel@polylink.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@polylink.com, Anika Sharma <anika.sharma@polylink.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion + multi-region capacity questions — tentative approval pending PO

Thanks, team.

Internal stakeholders have conditionally approved the amendment as described: 18-month term, EU (8 nodes) + APAC (6 nodes), 12% discount, capped cross-region egress at $6k/mo, and the 3-month ramp. We just need the amendment + DocuSign packet and a short failover runbook for our SREs to validate.

Next steps for Redwood:
- Send DocuSign amendment link (please include the cap and early-exit numbers Neha referenced).
- Share the failover_runbook_stub.txt and propose a 2-hour test window next week for traffic failover verification.
- Point of contact for signature/PO is Anika Sharma (anika.sharma@polylink.com).

Happy to move quickly once we have the DocuSign and the runbook.

Best,
Miguel
Head of Platform Engineering, Polylink Inc.
